page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this configuration provides 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It lacks local storage and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%, and average single-core scores in Geekbench. However, multi-core CPU performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for both stress-ng and Geekbench. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only small block cached bandwidth rated as poor and large block read/write bandwidth rated as weak.

Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance provides a high memory density per core, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing. It is suitable for lightweight database operations, text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, and basic web serving. However, it is poorly suited for compiler tasks, ray tracing, or heavy database operations, as reflected in its low Passmark database and clang compilation scores.
